entities.name: anthropic principle
entities.definition: The anthropic principle suggests that observed physical laws are constrained by our existence. It posits that if the universe's constants differed even slightly, life could not evolve to measure them.

entities.name: cosmological principle
entities.definition: The cosmological principle assumes that on large scales, the universe at any given time is identical everywhere. This fundamental concept implies that space is both isotropic and homogeneous throughout cosmic history.

entities.name: encapsulation
entities.definition: Encapsulation ensures that attributes and behaviors of classes remain self-contained throughout their lifetime. This principle binds data with its methods to restrict direct access from outside the object.

entities.name: Addition Principle
entities.definition: The Addition Principle states that if two mutually exclusive events occur in m and n ways respectively, the total number of outcomes for either event is their sum. This rule provides a fundamental method for counting possibilities when choices are distinct.
